Wind action is nearly constant in the region, and clay and siltsized particles loosened by blasting, digging, and grading will easily
become airborne. Soil particles will also be transported off-site by
surface water runoff. Soil erosion and deposition will be increased
where soil permeability and infiltration are reduced by compaction and
cementation. Any steep slopes left from mining excavations will be very
susceptable to water erosion.
Soils in the immediate vicinity of haul roads and processing facilities as well as along railroad lines may be adversely affected by settling of coal dust.
Hydrology
<u>Surface Water</u> - Mining on Tracts II and III will result in changes in the quantity, duration, and timing of surface-water discharging from the affected area. These changes will be caused by the following:
Interception of runoff in the mine pit.
Interception of runoff by reclaimed areas where runoff will infiltrate and be lost either to ground water or to evapotranspiration.
   Storage of runoff in detention ponds with resultant surface evaporation.
4. Consumptive use of water from detention ponds.
These factors will also reduce flood volumes and peak flows from precipitation and snowmelt in the watersheds controlled by each structure.
